title: Above average
prompt: Show the name and salary of employees earning more than the average salary. Replace the ___ with a subquery.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT name, salary FROM employees WHERE salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees);

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name, salary FROM employees WHERE salary > AVG(salary);
wrongSolutions.why: An aggregate can't go directly in WHERE

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name, salary FROM employees WHERE salary < (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees);

title: Most expensive book
prompt: Show the title of the book with the highest price, using a subquery.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM books; INSERT INTO books VALUES (10, 'Copper Moon', 'Ada Hill', 'Fantasy', 20.0, 100, 2020), (11, 'North Light', 'Raj Dev', 'Travel', 7.5, 180, 2015), (12, 'Sky Atlas', 'Ada Hill', 'Science', 25.0, 300, 2023);

solutions: SELECT title FROM books WHERE price = (SELECT MAX(price) FROM books);

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT title FROM books WHERE price = (SELECT MIN(price) FROM books);

title: Difference from average
prompt: Show each employee's name and salary minus the overall average, rounded to 2 decimals, as difference.
hints: A subquery can go in SELECT.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT name, ROUND(salary - (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees), 2) AS difference FROM employees;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name, salary AS difference FROM employees;
SELECT name, ROUND((SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees) - salary, 2) AS difference FROM employees;

title: Share of products
prompt: Show each category and its share of all products as a percentage, rounded to 1 decimal, as share.
hints: Divide by a subquery counting all products.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL); INSERT INTO products VALUES (10, 'Vase', 'Home', 5.0, 2.0);

solutions: SELECT category, ROUND(COUNT(*) * 100.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM products), 1) AS share FROM products GROUP BY category;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT category, ROUND(COUNT(*) * 100 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM products), 1) AS share FROM products GROUP BY category;
SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS share FROM products GROUP BY category;

title: When there's no answer
prompt: Show the highest salary below 30000 as salary. When none exists, the result should be one row containing NULL.
hints: A scalar subquery returns NULL when it finds nothing, but MAX alone does too.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test'); UPDATE employees SET salary = 29000 WHERE id = 14; UPDATE employees SET salary = 20000 WHERE id = 15;

solutions: SELECT MAX(salary) AS salary FROM employees WHERE salary < 30000;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT salary FROM employees WHERE salary < 30000 ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT 1;
wrongSolutions.why: Returns no rows instead of NULL

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT MIN(salary) AS salary FROM employees WHERE salary < 30000;

title: Fix the comparison
prompt: This should show employees earning the top salary, but it fails because the subquery returns a whole column. Fix it.
hints: = needs a single value, so use MAX.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE salary = (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM employees);

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE salary IN (SELECT salary FROM employees);
SELECT name FROM employees WHERE salary > (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM employees);

title: Above average session
prompt: Show the id and minutes of sessions longer than the average session.
solutions: SELECT id, minutes FROM sessions WHERE minutes > (SELECT AVG(minutes) FROM sessions);

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id, minutes FROM sessions WHERE minutes >= (SELECT MAX(minutes) FROM sessions);
SELECT id, minutes FROM sessions WHERE minutes < (SELECT AVG(minutes) FROM sessions);

title: Second-highest salary
prompt: Show the second-highest different salary as salary. If there isn't one, return one row containing NULL.
hints: Wrap a query with OFFSET in a scalar subquery.
solutions: SELECT (SELECT DISTINCT salary FROM employees ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1) AS salary;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT DISTINCT salary FROM employees ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1;
wrongSolutions.why: Returns no row instead of NULL

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT (SELECT salary FROM employees ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1) AS salary;
wrongSolutions.why: Ties can repeat the top salary
